definitions.explanation: Vinegar used in cooking. The polite prefix お makes this the standard everyday form; plain 酢 sounds blunt in conversation.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}にお{酢|す}を{少|すこ}し{入|い}れる。
examples.english: I add a little vinegar to the dish.

examples.japanese: お{酢|す}は{健康|けんこう}にいいと{言|い}われているので、{毎日|まいにち}{飲|の}んでいる。
examples.english: Vinegar is said to be good for your health, so I drink it every day.

notes: The polite prefix お is almost always used in everyday speech; plain {酢|す} appears mainly in compound words and technical contexts. Common collocations: お{酢|す}をかける (to put vinegar on), {酢|す}の{物|もの} (vinegared dish), {酢飯|すめし} (vinegared sushi rice). Types of vinegar: {米酢|こめず} (rice vinegar), {穀物酢|こくもつす} (grain vinegar), {黒酢|くろず} (black vinegar). Related: {酸|す}っぱい (sour — shares the same kanji root).
